title: Flat degree-zero scalar comparison agrees between module-object and ringed-site conventions
statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,J)$ be a site small in the chosen module universe [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention], let $\varphi:R\to B$ be a morphism of sheaves of commutative rings, and use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] with sheafified sectionwise tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Put $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ with tensor $\otimes_R$ and unit $R$. Regard $R$ as the unit monoid and $B$ as a commutative monoid of $\mathcal A$ via $\varphi$. Identify modules over the unit monoid with $\mathcal A$ by the unit action, and $B$-module objects of $\mathcal A$ with sheaves of $B$-modules by their given actions. Let $E_{\mathrm{mon}}$ be the coequalizer extension of [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars] under these identifications, and let $E_{\mathrm{sec}}(M)=B\otimes_R M$ have $B$ acting on the first factor. There is a natural $B$-linear isomorphism
$$e_M:E_{\mathrm{mon}}(M)\xrightarrow{\sim}E_{\mathrm{sec}}(M)$$
whose composite with the balancing-coequalizer projection is the identity on the local pure tensors $b\otimes m$.

Let $M$ be any flat $R$-module sheaf [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Then $M[0]$ is K-flat for the two-sided quasi-isomorphism convention [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso] as well as for the acyclic-total-tensor convention [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Use ordinary unbounded derived categories with localization functors $Q_R,Q_B$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For total left derived extensions $L E_{\mathrm{mon}}$ and $L E_{\mathrm{sec}}$ with their canonical comparison counits, interpreted respectively by [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories] and the ringed-site change of rings [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], let $e^{\mathbf L}:L E_{\mathrm{mon}}\xrightarrow{\sim}L E_{\mathrm{sec}}$ denote the comparison induced by $e$ and preserving these counits. The degree-zero comparisons $c_{\mathrm{mon},M}$ and $c_{\mathrm{sec},M}$, each directed from the derived extension of $Q_R(M[0])$ to $Q_B((E(M))[0])$, are isomorphisms and satisfy
$$c_{\mathrm{sec},M}\circ e^{\mathbf L}_{Q_R(M[0])}=Q_B(e_M[0])\circ c_{\mathrm{mon},M}.$$
This equality is natural for morphisms between flat module sheaves. No local freeness of $M$ and no flatness of $B$ over $R$ is assumed.
